scope: Theorem 6.1 (Analytic score gap) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 117 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 75f6af00a38589bf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each fixed T0 ≥ 1, the primitive system of Section 4 admits a demand law µ of scores and a finite sum D of raw comparison forms with the following properties. All arities, score bounds, numerical dimensions, and total comparison weight are bounded by constants independent of the input size. The laws and weights do not depend on a lookup. At a perfect witness x, Z |B(x) − B′ (x)| dm(B, B′ ) ≤ 4, µ{B : B(x) ≥ 1/4}, µ{B : B(x) ≤ −1/4} ≥ 10−4 . In a NO instance, every binary measurable lookup with ν = Varµ(h) > 0 satisfies D(h) > T0ν. Conditional on the discrete sampling data, the numerical laws and score entries belong to fixed finite families of polynomials with rational coefficients on rational boxes, with atoms represented as separate cases.
